newsitem.title: BOSNIA: OSCE figures show Izetbegovic topping Bosnia poll.
newsitem.headline: OSCE figures show Izetbegovic topping Bosnia poll.

text.p: With most of the votes counted in Bosnia's elections, figures released by international organisers show Moslem leader Alija Izetbegovic winning the contest to head a national three-man presidency.

The Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) said that with 86 out of 89 counting stations in the Moslem-Croat Federation reporting, Izetbegovic had 699,586 votes. His Bosnian Serb rival Momcilo Krajisnik had 631,767 votes from 59 out of 61 counting stations in the Serb Republic.
Both men are well ahead of their respective rivals for the Moslem and Serb seats in the rotating presidency in which the overall winner becomes the first chairman.

The OSCE figures showed that Krajisnik's main challenger, Mladen Ivanic, had taken 282,985 votes in a stronger than expected showing, while former prime minister Haris Silajdzic polled only 121,253 votes in the race for the Moslem seat.
Croat nationalist leader Kresimir Zubak had polled 331,133 votes against 36,913 for rival Ivo Komsic in the fight for the Croat seat.
The OSCE said more than 1.2 million people had voted in the federation and 938,500 in the semi-autonomous Serb Republic, but cautioned that some results were missing.
